## Summary

A one-parameter exponential cooling model fitted to the example observations
gives {{< meta cooling-fit.rate >}} ({{< meta cooling-fit.time-constant >}}),
with a residual RMSE of {{< meta cooling-fit.rmse >}}
(@tbl-cooling-parameters).

::: {.callout-important}
## Numerical checks: {{< meta cooling-fit.checks >}}
The checks verify the fit to these observations. The observations have no
measurement record, so the result demonstrates the method and is not a
physical validation.
:::

## Model

The temperature excess over ambient decays at a rate proportional to itself
[@newton1701], giving

$$
T(t) = T_a + (T_0 - T_a)\,e^{-k t},
$$ {#eq-cooling-model}

where $T$ and the fixed inputs $T_a$ and $T_0$ are in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, $t$ is
in $\mathrm{s}$, and $k$ is in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

::: {.column-margin}
The time constant $1/k$ is the time for the temperature excess $T - T_a$ to
fall by a factor of $e$.
:::

The rate $k$ solves the bounded least-squares problem[^solver]

$$
\hat{k} = \arg\min_{k \ge 0} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left[T(t_i; k) - T_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\right]^2
$$ {#eq-fit-objective}

over the $n =$ {{< meta cooling-fit.observations >}} observations, using
@eq-cooling-model for $T(t_i; k)$.

[^solver]: SciPy's trust-region reflective method [@branch1999; @virtanen2020],
    started from two initial guesses to check that the optimum does not depend
    on the start.

## Limitations

The linearized standard error of {{< meta cooling-fit.rate-standard-error >}}
omits uncertainty in $T_a$ and $T_0$, and the observations have no recorded
measurement uncertainty. The analysis notebook lists the retained files, their
hashes, and the model source.
